correctness.rationale: Two edge-disjoint paths between the minimum and maximum of every one-Lipschitz function give at least two arclength units of preimage per unit level interval. This proves the exact \(L/2\)-Lipschitz output quantile bound. Its centered quantile is majorized by a linearly increasing uniform quantile, proving convex order for every convex test. Strict-convexity equality forces the uniform law, and the diameter bound and two-geodesic exhaustion yield exactly the distance-from-diametral-point maximizers. Conversely such distance maps attain equality. Exact rational checker on 264 bridgeless graphs and explicit boundary examples corroborates but is not used for the general proof.

value.rationale: An all-convex ordering simultaneously resolves variance, all exponential moments and every centered absolute moment for all finite bridgeless length networks, not a single graph or moment. The iff diameter saturation and complete strict-convexity optimizer classification distinguish circumference-like graphs from theta graphs, while a bridge path gives a genuine structural failure. This is a natural functional-analytic embedding and concentration statement; the specific two-route lower level-mass mechanism is mathematically substantive.
